title: Ireland – Software package and information systems – UL1084 Enterprise-level Systematic Review Management Platform to the University of Limerick
description: University of Limerick is seeking to procure an enterprise-level, cloud-based Systematic Review Management Platform to support researchers, academics, students, librarians and research support staff in conducting high-quality evidence synthesis activities across the institution. The proposed solution must provide an integrated end-to-end workflow for systematic reviews and related evidence synthesis methodologies, including citation management, screening, full-text review, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, collaboration, reporting and publication-ready outputs. The platform should facilitate efficient collaboration between internal and external researchers, provide enterprise-grade administration and reporting capabilities, and support recognised methodologies such as systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid reviews, mixed-methods reviews and meta-analyses. The successful Tenderer will be required to deliver a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, including implementation, training, ongoing support, systematic review methodological expertise, security and compliance assurances, and enterprise-level service management. The solution must align with the University's information governance, security, accessibility and architectural requirements, while providing value for money and supporting the University's strategic ambition to strengthen research excellence and evidence-informed decision-making across the institution.

title: RRSA 20V1163TB93L Diesel Engine Disassembly and Parts Harvesting
description: The U.S. Coast Guard has a one-time requirement for services associated with four MTU series 20V1163TB93L diesel engines currently stored at a Rolls-Royce Solutions America facility in Brownstown, Michigan. The requirement includes the following major tasks: Transport and complete disassembly of four MTU 20V1163TB93L diesel engines. Salvage of usable spare parts to support the National Security Cutter fleet. Salvage of all four crankshafts. Modification of two salvaged crankshafts to the current approved/improved radius design. Cleaning, preservation, packaging, and marking of salvaged components for long-term storage and future fleet use. Preservation, sealing, packaging, and shipment of two bare engine blocks for long-term strategic storage. Scrapping and disposal of two bare engine blocks. Inventory, sorting, preservation, and disposition of parts contained in Government-owned conex sea containers. Shipment of project deliverables FOB Destination to Government-designated locations. The engines identified for disassembly are: Engine Serial Number 5840363 Engine Serial Number 5840364 Engine Serial Number 5840397 Engine Serial Number 5840401 The salvaged parts will support sustainment of the U.S. Coast Guard National Security Cutter Main Propulsion Diesel Engines. title: Freeze Dry System- Brand Name or Equal -Brand Name and Equal (BNE)
description: Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The NAICS for this requirement is: 334516. The government is not obligated to make an award. The Government is not obligated to pay costs incurred by the Contractor during quote preparation and quote submission. Background: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) laboratory requires a benchtop freeze dryer (lyophilizer) system to support ongoing scientific research and sample preservation activities. Lyophilization (freeze-drying) is a critical process used to preserve the stability and integrity of biological samples, pharmaceuticals, and other moisture-sensitive materials by removing water content through sublimation under vacuum. The required system must achieve a collector temperature of -84 �C or colder to accommodate samples with lower freezing points, including those containing organic solvents. The system must be configured for 230V/50-60 Hz operation consistent with the FDA laboratory's electrical infrastructure. Minimum Performance Requirements/Salient Characteristics: This is a Brand Name or Equal requirement. Products other than the aforementioned are acceptable but shall meet all the salient characteristics contained in the Minimum Technical Requirements below: All of the following system requirements are minimum requirements. Equivalent requirements that differ from these minimum requirements shall be justified by the proposing vendor and evaluated prior to purchase: General The contractor shall provide One (1) benchtop freeze dryer (lyophilizer) system meeting the following minimum technical specifications, including all required accessories, tubing, clamps, adapters, and standard warranty necessary for full system assembly and operation: � Collector Temperature: -84 �C or colder (to accommodate samples containing organic solvents such as acetonitrile or methanol) � Collector Capacity: Approximately 2.5 liters of ice capacity before defrost cycle � Condenser Type: Stainless steel or PTFE-coated coils (corrosion-resistant construction) � Drying Chamber: 12-port drying chamber or manifold for simultaneous multi-sample processing � Accessories: Initial set of flasks (150 mL and 300 mL), all necessary tubing, clamps, and adapters required for full system assembly � Electrical: 230V, 50/60 Hz configuration Place of Performance: The prospective vendor should provide insured shipping of equipment to: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Attn: Kyung Sung 10903 New Hampshire Ave, Building 52/72. Room 3248 Silver Spring, MD 20993 Period of Performance: Performance begins on the date of formal government acceptance and continues through the end of the manufacturer's warranty period. Quotes are due by email on or before September 28 2026, by 12:00 P.M. (Eastern Standard Time) and should be sent to brandon.rafus@fda.hhs.gov.

The objective is to provide farmers with information about how to achieve the best planting results and subsequent crop yield following grain corn, which produces large amounts of crop residue. A shredder is needed that lifts fallen corn residue and shred all residue to a size that facilitates tillage operations and promotes residue decomposition in a semi-arid area with cold, dry winters.

Responses to this notice shall include company name, size status for the above reference NAICS code, a descriptive service capability statement, System for Award Management (SAM) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, address, point of contact, and examples of similar facilities to which services have been provided. Contractors should provide information on whether they are certified SDVOSB, VOSB, Hub zone, 8(a), women-owned concern, or other. If standard company brochures will be provided as a response to this Source Sought, ensure that additional information tailored to this notice is included. If a solicitation is issued, it will be announced on the Contract Opportunities website https://sam.gov/ at a later date, and all interested parties must respond to that solicitation announcement separately from the response to this announcement. Specific areas to be addressed in capability packages submitted by respondents are as follows: 1. Capability Statements: If considering subcontracting, state so in your response and include subcontractor information, including SAM UEI and name. 2. Evidence of applicable certifications, licenses, and permits from federal, state, and local agencies applicable to the industry in Puerto Rico. If subcontracting, include subcontractor licenses and certifications as well. 3. Provide enough information to sustain your level of experience in the maintenance and repair services of steam boilers, having certified oil burner technicians for combustion and Cleaver-Brooks trained/certified personnel, and any other compelling evidence to help the Government determine your company's capabilities. 4. If you are a GSA contract holder, please provide the schedule and contract number. Responses to this notice must be submitted to Aurea.Gonzalez@va.gov no later than September 28, 2026 at 1:00 PM AST. Telephone and facsimile inquiries will not be considered. No other information is available at this time.

title: Base ATV, UTV and Snowmachine Maintenance and Repair
description: PURPOSE: The purpose of the sources sought is to identify available authorized businesses to provide ATV, UTV, and snowmobile- diagnostics, maintenance and repair at Fairchild AFB. This sources sought notice is for informational and planning purposes only. Pricing information is not being requested at this time. It does not constitute a solicitation and is not to be considered as a commitment by the government. REQUIREMENT: This notice is issued by the U.S. Air Force, 92d Contracting Squadron, Fairchild AFB, WA. This sources sought is seeking to identify responsible potential sources to provide diagnostics, maintenance and repair for ATV, UTV, and snowmobile vehicles at Fairchild AFB. The base-wide ATV, UTV, and snowmobile- diagnostics, maintenance and repair services must meet the specifications in accordance with the attached Statement of Work. ANTICIPATED NAICS/SIZE STANDARD: This requirement falls under the NAICS Code of 811111, General Automotive Repair, a size standard of $9.00M. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION: All firms responding to this sources sought notice are advised that their response to this notice is not a request that will be considered for contract award. All interested parties will be required to respond to the resultant solicitation separately from their response to this sources sought notice. A responsible potential source shall have registered with the System for Award Management (SAM). The response should be no more than five pages providing the following information: Specifications of the ATV, UTV, and snowmobile- diagnostics, maintenance and repair services Provide feedback on what areas of the Statement of Work your company can complete and areas your company cannot complete Business name, address, CAGE code Size and socioeconomic classification based on NAICS size standard If claiming a specific small business category, provide supporting documentation Point of contact including email and phone number Please respond to this request by 28 September 2026 at 10:00 AM Pacific Time Attachment 1: 26QA297 SOW Draft

title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Contractor to Review and Revise the Patent Examiner Training program.
description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION � PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO�s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. REQUIREMENTS: Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing innovative solutions including AI to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to refine learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course pedagogy for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to guide the assessment of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. As directed, develop training content and related deliverables. Development of eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of eLearning content, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, etc. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building in adaptive gamification into eLearning content. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Experience in incorporating clean visuals, graphics, and ensuring 508-compliance of all materials. Experience in graphic design, visual clarity, and technical writing to ensure clear instructions and flow of all eLearning content. Experience in intuitive, learner-centered design. Experience in clearly defining design processes, to include steps in design processes, timelines, and checkpoints for subject-matter expert review. Ability to convert 25 courses into eLearning modules in 3 months. Courses range from 1 hour to 2.5 hours� worth of content. Training Delivery Support Services: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the implementation of Training Delivery Support Services, to include: Experience providing training in person and online, using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Experience in ensuring best practices in engagement and adult learning theory are incorporated into training delivery. Ability to deliver training on all agency examination processes, procedures and tools accessing patent applications, in-house tools for searching US and Foreign Patents that allow examiners to generate correspondence to applicants, case management tools. Ability to deliver professional training that is consistent with USPTO standards to support professional development to USPTO patent examiner employees. The training must be conducted by a variety of means including in person, in a classroom or lecture setting, and/or using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Please state if you have specific experience with intellectual property (IP), patent examination, and patent prosecution processes. Experience in ensuring continuity in training to avoid re-scheduling of training classes. The ability to ensure training coverage for a schedule such as the one listed below: Phase 1 Week 1 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 2 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 3 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 4 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 5 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 6 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 7 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 8 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 9 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 10 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days PROGRAM TIMELINE Contractors would be expected to begin delivering consultation services in October 2026, with an expectation of revised training program initiatives to begin implementation in January 2027. General responses with generic capability statements that do not address the specific content of this RFI may not be considered. description: THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. REQUEST FOR A SOLICITATION WILL NOT RECEIVE A RESPONSE. This Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) is in support of Market Research being conducted by the Defense Logistics Agency to identify potential manufacturing/supply sources, and if future efforts can be competitive or Set Aside for Small Business. The proposed North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 332510 which has a corresponding Size Standard of 750 employees. This SSS is to notify companies that the Defense Logistics Agency, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is seeking qualified sources for the acquisition of a HOOK,CARGO, NSN: 4030-01-187-0900, Part Number: 145ES102- 5 in support of the CHINOOK weapon system. The rights to use the data needed to purchase this part from additional source(s) are not owned by the Government and cannot be purchased, developed, or otherwise obtained. It is uneconomical to reverse engineer this part. As a result, this acquisition is currently being procured under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302- 1(a)(1) having only a limited number of responsible sources. The Government is interested in all businesses to include 8(a), small business and small disadvantaged business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Hubzone, and Women-Owned small business concerns. All contractors must meet prequalification requirements in order to be registered as a potential source. Firms that possess the ability and can produce the required item(s) described above are encouraged to identify themselves. Contractors are encouraged to seek source approval in order to compete for future solicitations by visiting AvMC's public website: https://amrdec.army.afpims.mil/Directorates/STI/ The contractor shall be capable of successfully performing and complying with any and all special requirements in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the solicitation annotated above, at the unit prices established at time of a contract award. The contractor will be responsible for recurring and nonrecurring engineering services associated with becoming a qualified source. The contractor will also be responsible for all aspects of the manufacturing/production process, including but not limited to: supply chain management, logistics, forecasting of parts, long-lead parts procurement, material forecasting, obsolescence issues and final delivery of assets as well as any and all additional costs incurred resulting from contract performance. DISCLAIMER: THIS SSS IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATIONAL AND PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION (REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL OR REQUEST FOR QUOTATION) OR A PROMISE TO ISSUE A SOLICITATION IN THE FUTURE AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Integrated Sustainment for Item Unique Identification (IUID) Marking Systems Fleet Contracting Activity: AFSC OL:H/PZIEA Anticipated NAICS: 811310 Anticipated PSC/FSC: J036 Response Due Date: 28 September 2026 NOTICE: This is not a solicitation. 1. This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) / Market Survey conducted pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 (Market Research). This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or solicitation, nor does it represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. 2. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. 3. No Reimbursement: The Government will not reimburse any interested party for costs incurred in preparing, submitting, or providing information in response to this synopsis, nor for any follow-up information or discussions. All participation is strictly voluntary and at the respondent�s expense. 4. Purpose: The Government will use the market research information obtained via this Sources Sought to determine the most advantageous acquisition strategy, identify potential prime contractors, assess small business capabilities, evaluate competition, and determine the feasibility of socioeconomic set-asides for the procurement of total integrated sustainment for the AFSC fleet of sixty (60) IUID marking systems in support of the Air Force IUID Program. REQUIREMENT The Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC) requires total integrated sustainment for its geographically distributed fleet of sixty (60) Item Unique Identification (IUID) marking systems. The Air Force IUID Program ensures end-to-end asset visibility, inventory accountability, and lifecycle traceability for critical weapon system parts and depot-level repairables across the Air Force logistics complex. description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION � PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO�s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. REQUIREMENTS: Training Consultation for Program Revision: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in instructional design consultation services, to include: Expertise in instructional design and adult learning theories and principles. Experience providing solutions to enhance engagement and learning in large training programs with extensive curriculums, specifically more than 40 courses in a single curriculum. Experience with providing innovative solutions including AI to enhance learning and taking complex, detailed curriculum and transforming the curriculum to provide faster acquisition of job skills and application of content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to refine learning objectives and ensure content alignment with learning objectives for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course activities for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to review and revise course pedagogy for highly complex legal and examination procedure topics. Ability to work with subject matter experts to guide the assessment of learning objectives and outcomes. Experience in providing consultation services for legal content. As directed, develop training content and related deliverables. Development of eLearning Content: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the development and implementation of eLearning content, to include: Expertise in the design of eLearning content, using standard eLearning authoring tools such as Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, etc. Expertise in incorporating instructional design and adult learning theories and principles to eLearning content. Experience in building in adaptive gamification into eLearning content. Experience in designing microlearning content. Ability to work with subject matter experts to ensure the design correctly represents legally accurate materials. Experience in incorporating clean visuals, graphics, and ensuring 508-compliance of all materials. Experience in graphic design, visual clarity, and technical writing to ensure clear instructions and flow of all eLearning content. Experience in intuitive, learner-centered design. Experience in clearly defining design processes, to include steps in design processes, timelines, and checkpoints for subject-matter expert review. Ability to convert 25 courses into eLearning modules in 3 months. Courses range from 1 hour to 2.5 hours� worth of content. Training Delivery Support Services: The USPTO seeks firms with experience in the implementation of Training Delivery Support Services, to include: Experience providing training in person and online, using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Experience in ensuring best practices in engagement and adult learning theory are incorporated into training delivery. Ability to deliver training on all agency examination processes, procedures and tools accessing patent applications, in-house tools for searching US and Foreign Patents that allow examiners to generate correspondence to applicants, case management tools. Ability to deliver professional training that is consistent with USPTO standards to support professional development to USPTO patent examiner employees. The training must be conducted by a variety of means including in person, in a classroom or lecture setting, and/or using agency collaboration tools such as MS Teams. Please state if you have specific experience with intellectual property (IP), patent examination, and patent prosecution processes. Experience in ensuring continuity in training to avoid re-scheduling of training classes. The ability to ensure training coverage for a schedule such as the one listed below: Phase 1 Week 1 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 2 8:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 3 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 4 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days) Week 5 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 6 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 7 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 8 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days Week 9 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) Friday Off Week 10 7:30 a.m. � 5:00 p.m. ET (9-hour days) FRIDAY 7:30 a.m. � 4:30 p.m. ET (8-hour days PROGRAM TIMELINE Contractors would be expected to begin delivering consultation services in October 2026, with an expectation of revised training program initiatives to begin implementation in January 2027. title: Think Trends Software Implementation and Support
description: ThinkTrends Software Implementation and Support IDIQ The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) hereby issues Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 75F40126R00097 for ThinkTrends Software Implementation and Support services. The Government intends to award one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to provide technical and programmatic services supporting the implementation, integration, enhancement, maintenance, licensing support, and sustainment of the ThinkTrends software environment across FDA operations. The resulting contract will provide a contractual vehicle through which FDA may issue task orders for specific requirements within the scope of the IDIQ. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside pursuant to FAR 19.502-2(b). The applicable NAICS code is 541511 � Custom Computer Programming Services, with a size standard of $34 million in average annual receipts. Only eligible small business concerns meeting the applicable requirements of the solicitation may submit proposals. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The contractor shall provide comprehensive technical expertise to support ThinkTrends software implementation and related activities across FDA operations. The requirement includes, but is not limited to: ThinkTrends software implementation, configuration, enhancement, maintenance, and support; Application and system integration; Data migration, integration, cleansing, cataloging, and engineering; Document AI, OCR, ICR, and NLP capabilities; RPA and intelligent workflow automation; AI/ML lifecycle management and related MLOps activities; Analytics, visualization, dashboards, and decision-support capabilities; Digitization and conversion of regulatory documents and adverse event reports; Integration with FDA systems and data sources; Application development and enhancement; Security, compliance, validation, auditability, and operational support; Agile project and program management; Training and knowledge transfer; Transition and continuity-of-operations support; and ThinkTrends software license acquisition and installation support, as applicable to individual task orders. Specific requirements and performance standards are provided in Section C � Statement of Work and the other solicitation documents. EXISTING THINKTRENDS ENVIRONMENT FDA currently utilizes ThinkTrends capabilities in certain regulatory tools and systems, including the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), Site Selection Tools, and the BIMO Evaluation Support Tool (BEST). Performance under the resulting contract will require the successful offeror to work within the Government's existing ThinkTrends environment and applicable FDA technical, security, data, integration, and operational environments. Where performance requires software licenses, proprietary technical information, platform access, interfaces, documentation, or other third-party-controlled resources, the contractor shall obtain and maintain all rights, licenses, permissions, access, and authorizations necessary to perform the contract requirements. Offerors shall address their approach to obtaining and maintaining any such resources as required by the solicitation.

title: Interactive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Training Platform Development
description: Request for Information (RFI) & Sources Sought (pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulations- Part 5) Interactive Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) Training Platform Development Issued By: Department of Transportation | Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Date of Issue: September 9, 2026 Response Deadline: September 28, 2026 SIC/Product Service Code: 7373 Computer Integrated Systems NAICS Code: 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services 1. Introduction The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) is seeking information from interested parties and potential vendors regarding the development of an Interactive LNG Training Platform. The interactive, virtual LNG plant training platform should allow users to perform virtual plant walkdowns, review piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), and visualize process flows through the internal components of critical machinery (e.g., valves, vessels, pumps, compressors). This RFI is intended for market research purposes only and supports ongoing agency acquisition planning aligned with modern federal procurement principles. 2. Project Background and Goals PHMSA is committed to enhancing the safety and oversight of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) facilities. The objective of this project is to create a digital, high-fidelity, and interactive training environment that allows inspectors to simulate complex operational scenarios and safety inspections. Key goals include: Improving technical competency in LNG facility oversight. Utilizing 3D immersive technologies and digital twin capabilities to bridge the gap between classroom and field. Creating a scalable, modular curriculum that evolves with regulatory standards. Maximizing the leverage of commercial solutions and modern cloud infrastructure. 3. Key Information Requested PHMSA requests that interested respondents provide detailed information on the following categories: 3.1 Company Profile & Administrative Information Please complete the following table to assist PHMSA in market research and business size determination: Company Name Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE Code Socioeconomic Business Size (e.g., SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone, Small, Large) Point of Contact Information (Name, Email, Phone) [Vendor Name] [12-character UEI] [5-charac ter CAGE] t[Socioeconomic Status] [Name, Email, Phone] Small Business Capacity: If identified as a small business, please state whether your firm possesses the internal capacity and capability to perform as the prime contractor for a project of this scope or if teaming/subcontracting arrangements would be necessary. 3.2 Technical Capabilities & Innovation Describe your firm�s experience in developing high-fidelity 3D simulations or "Digital Twins" for industrial facilities. What hardware and software requirements do you typically recommend for a platform of this scale? Explain your approach to ensuring interactivity and user engagement within a training module. Commerciality & COTS Analysis: To what extent can your proposed solution leverage existing Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software components, modular training engines, or commercial 3D/VR frameworks versus requiring custom government-unique software development? 3.3 Content and Curriculum Design How do you approach mapping technical regulatory requirements (e.g., 49 CFR Part 193) into interactive learning objectives? Describe your capability to develop branching scenarios where trainee decisions lead to different safety outcomes. 3.4 Cybersecurity, Hosting & Data Rights Deployment & Cloud Posture: Describe your solution's typical deployment model (e.g., SaaS, FedRAMP-authorized Cloud, On-Premise, Hybrid) and compatibility with federal cybersecurity frameworks (FAR Part 40 / CUI handling). Intellectual Property & Licensing: Describe your standard licensing structure and approach to data rights for custom-developed 3D models, code, and scenario content (e.g., proprietary licensing vs. Government Purpose Rights / Unlimited Rights). 3.5 Past Performance Please provide details on up to three (3) recent projects of similar scope and complexity: Project Title Client Type (Gov/Private) Core Technology Used Year Completed [Project 1] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 2] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] [Project 3] [Gov/Private] [Tech Stack / Engines] [Year] 3.6 Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) and Timeline Provide a non-binding estimate of the typical timeline for developing a comprehensive training platform with 5�10 high-complexity modules. Outline standard pricing models (e.g., fixed-price development, recurring licensing fees, maintenance, and ongoing support). 4. Submission Instructions & Industry Engagement Responses should be submitted in electronic format to the point of contact listed below. Please limit technical responses to 20 pages, excluding company brochures or supplemental past performance data. Industry Engagement / Vendor Demos: PHMSA may, at its discretion, invite select respondents to participate in virtual demonstrations or technical exchange sessions to further inform agency acquisition planning. USDOT Point of Contact: Loni Chinn Email: loni.chinn@dot.gov 5. Disclaimer: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. PHMSA will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI.

title: TR-143A TRANSDUCERS
description: ITEM DESCRIPTION - Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane (NSWC Crane) has a requirement to procure TR-143A Transducers, Part Number: 7146100-302. These transducers are utilized in the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem, supporting United States (U.S) Navy and United Kingdom (UK) Ballistic Missile Submarine Nuclear Powered submarines as part of the Navigation Subsystem Sonar. These transducers are used in coordination with TR-333 Hydrophones to receive signals from the ocean floor and to improve submarine launch accuracy. The transducers are manufactured items used as replacement assets during normal refit, replenish, and replacement operations for the SP24 Trident Navigation Subsystem and support U.S. Ohio and Columbia class submarines in addition to UK Vanguard and Dreadnought class submarines. The proposed contract action is for a two-year ordering period extension and ceiling increase, on contract N0016426DGP87, a firm-fixed-price, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract with a five-year ordering period. The contract is for supplies which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with one source, Massa Products Corporation, Hingham, MA 02043 (CAGE 88958), under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (c) (2), only one responsible source. The requirement is being solicited on a sole source basis, because the supplies have been deemed to be available only from the original source in the case of a follow-on contract for the continued production of highly specialized equipment, including major components thereof, when it is likely that award to any other source would result in (A) Substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition or (B) Unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Additionally, the Government is pursuing a sole source procurement to mitigate associated certification costs and certification testing that can take up to thirty-six months to complete. Furthermore, if a potential vendor is not capable of meeting the certification requirements, there is high likelihood that ship schedules will be significantly impacted. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract extension based upon responses to the solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov.

description: Update (22 September 2026): The purpose of this update is to: 1. Post Amendment 0001 to the RFQ, extending the response due date. Please continue to monitor SAM.gov for updates and any additional information as it becomes available. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - The Commander, Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to PerkinElmer U.S. LLC, 710 Bridgeport AVE, Shelton, CT 06484-4797 (CAGE: 9G526) on a sole source basis in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.102(a), only one source reasonably available and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Materials Engineering Division (MED) at Fleet Readiness Center Southeast (FRCSE) has a requirement to procure a highly specialized, portable, and fully integrated Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) system. Fourier Transform � Infrared Spectroscopy is a critical characterization technique used to obtain infrared spectra of small molecules, polymeric, and composite materials in liquid and solid phases. The existing legacy spectrometer is aged and commercially obsolete, with ongoing system deterioration and the lack of manufacturer support preclude the MED�s ability to guarantee the accuracy and reliability of critical analytical results. Securing a replacement system is paramount, as this instrument is a mission-essential tool required to conduct urgent, point-of-need chemical analysis and material identification directly on the floor of the Aviation Composites Repair facility. The operational environment is characterized by the presence of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and suspended conductive particulates generated during composite repair and painting/coating operations. Due to the significant risk of electrical arcing and ignition in these spaces, an instrument with a low-voltage optical design is mandatory to comply with Navy Safety and Occupational Health (SOH) program guidelines. The primary objective for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) procurement of one complete, turnkey, portable Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectrometer system utilizing a low voltage laser design. The system must possess specific salient safety and operational characteristics to allow for safe operation within a hazardous industrial environment. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within four (4) calendar days after the date of the publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Pre-solicitation Notice: RRC Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines
description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000014 Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement radius 150-mile not restricted by State or County lines. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 14 beds (12 males and 2 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 35 beds (30 males and 5 females) facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 25 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000014 will be available on or about September 29, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around November 30, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

description: Request for Proposal (RFP) - 15BRRC26R00000014 Residential Reentry Center Services to be Located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement Radius 150-mile not Restricted by State or County Lines The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes which to be located within the Tennessee Counties of Carter, Cocke, Greene, Hamblen, Hancock, Hawkins, Johnson, Sullivan, Unicoi, and Washington. Home Confinement radius 150-mile not restricted by State or County lines. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March, 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the aforementioned SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four, one-year option period. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 14 beds (12 males and 2 females) for the base year and an estimated maximum 35 beds (30 males and 5 females) for female facility. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 10 placements (for the base year) and an estimated maximum 25 placements. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. 15BRRC26R00000014 will be available on or about September 29, 2026, and it will be distributed solely through the General Services Administration's Federal Business Opportunities website at https://SAM.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. Future information about this acquisition will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. The estimated closing date of this solicitation (RFP) will be after 60 days around November 30, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

title: Crisis Action Team (CAT) Audio/Visual (A/V) and Security Surveillance System Inspection, Preventive Maintenance, Training, and Service Agreement
description: This notice is a Notice of Intent to Award a Sole-Source Contract (Synopsis) published pursuant to RFO Subpart 5.1 and RFO Part 12. It does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or a commitment to issue a competitive solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. The Department of the Air Force intends to negotiate and award a sole-source contract to Pavion (formerly CTSI) for a 1-year comprehensive service, maintenance, and training agreement for the 72 ABW Crisis Action Team (CAT) Audio/Visual (A/V) and Video Surveillance Systems at Tinker AFB. The installed system architecture incorporates custom-compiled control software, uncompiled source code, and integration configurations owned exclusively by Pavion. Market research confirms that Pavion is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling this requirement without causing unrecoverable mission delays, system vulnerabilities, or unacceptable cost duplication due to proprietary software lock-in. Scope of Work Includes: - Onsite Preventative Maintenance and Training Call: Inspection, firmware updates, minor repairs using technician-stocked parts and cable and system calibration. - Maintenance Plan: Subsequent annual maintenance covering all parts and labor for all products in the systems (detailed in Attachment 1 of the PWS), regardless of whether originally provided by the installing contractor or by the Government. This includes onsite maintenance, user training, help-desk support, and onsite troubleshooting. - Emergency and Non-Emergency On-Call Support: On-call troubleshooting and rapid physical response. Capability Statements / Responses: This is a non-competitive action; however, any responsible source that believes it can fulfill the requirement without infringing upon proprietary software constraints or causing unacceptable technical risk may submit a Capability Statement (max 5 pages). Submissions must detail company business size/socioeconomic status under NAICS 334310, CAGE code, technical capability/OEM authorization to service this specific A/V configuration, and relevant past performance. Response Due Date: September 28, 2026, 13:00 CST Points of Contact: Rachael Thomas (rachael.thomas.3@us.af.mil) and Samuel Nemargut (samuel.nemargut@us.af.mil).

title: Technical Data and Support Services
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify vendors capable of supporting the Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) Command Fleet Readiness Center (COMFRC) Headquarters (HQ) Logistics Technical Data Department. This RFI is designed to assess industry capability, gather feedback on proposed acquisition strategies, and refine the upcoming procurement approach in accordance with the draft Statement of Objectives (SOO). This is a Request for Information (RFI)/Sources Sought only. There is no solicitation available at this time. The RFI is issued for the purpose of conducting Market Research in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 10. Additionally, the Government is interested in questions/comments/feedback on the SOO. We anticpate a five-year contract. The submission of information is for planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to procure any items or services. Draft SOO is attached. The information will not be returned, and no compensation will be provided from any response to this announcement. Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked. title: EADS MASS NOTIFCIATION SYSTEM TESTING & PREVENATIVE MAINTENANCE
description: This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote from the 174th Attack Wing, Syracuse, NY, with performance in Rome, NY. This solicitation is to perform preventative maintenance checks on the Mass Notification System at the Eastern Air Defense Sector (EADS), Rome, NY, as outlined in the attached PWS. The Eastern Air Defense Sector requires annual preventative maintenance for its Outdoor Mass Notification System to ensure its operational readiness and reliability. The system is critical for base-wide alerts and communication. The period of performance shall consist of one 12 month base year and four 12 month option years. **A site visit will be held Tuesday, 23 SEPT at 10:30am- please send required information to richard.peirson@us.af.mil and briana.mccaffery@us.af.mil** (send site visit attendee Name, Date of Birth, Driver�s License # and State of issue to shayne.stein@us.af.mil and nicholas.amicucci.1@us.af.mil) Site visit attendees will meet in the upper parking lot of the EADS instalation. Award will be made to the lowest price offer that can meet the criteria of the RFQ and PWS that is a small business registered in sam.gov. This is a total small business set aside under NAICS 561621. Vendors must provide a quote for ALL option years required. Partial quotes will not be considered. Quotes utilizing the SF 1449 attached are due 28 Sept 2026 at 2:00 pm via email to richard.peirson@us.af.mil and briana.mccaffery@us.af.mil. In order to be eligible for award, the successful offeror's System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) registration must be active and includes representations and certifications. The solicitation and all amendments are on www.Sam.Gov Contracting Opportunities. CAUTION: This solicitation will be issued electronically as will any amendments thereto. Because of this, the Government is under no obligation and is in fact unable to maintain a bidder's mailing list. It is therefore incumbent upon any interested parties to periodically access the above Internet address in order to obtain any amendments that may be issued. Failure to obtain any said amendments and to respond to them prior to the date and time set for receipt of offers may render your offer nonresponsive and result in the rejection of same. All questions on this posting and quotes must be submitted electronically via e-mail to richard.peirson@us.af.mil and briana.mccaffery@us.af.mil.

title: Sole Source Bioconscientia
description: Presolicitation and Notice of Intent to Sole Source The US Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) ERDC-EL Biotechnology Team requires advanced R&D support to investigate and advance synthetic biology tools. The overall objective is to develop, optimize, and validate platforms that address environmental sensing, critical material supply chain security, and sustainable biomanufacturing. The required tasks encompass: Project A: Development of synthetic cell systems for sensing physical and chemical stimuli via two-component signaling (TCS). Project B: Molecular engineering of CO2-utilizing yeast via AI-optimized Rubisco variants for austere biomanufacturing. Project C: Design and testing of engineered protein chromatography platforms for selective capture of Rare Earth Elements (REE). Project D: Development of genetically encoded conductive protein nanowires for bio-electronic sensing and energy assimilation. Optional Projects E & F: Bio-functionalized carbon quantum dot sensing platforms (including biodefense surrogates) and microbiologically induced calcite precipitation for geotechnical applications. Bioconscientia, LLC possesses highly specialized, unique capabilities and proprietary institutional knowledge essential to executing this complex portfolio of synthetic biology research. title: Cooperative Driving Automation (CDA) Small-Scale Industry Prototype
description: UPDATE: On August 24, 2026 a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) amendment was issued, see amended BAA in the attachments section titled "693JJ3-26-BAA-0005_A00001_CDA Prototype". Additionally, the complete Q&A was posted as a PDF titled "Q A - Complete". Note that the due date for proposals was extended. BACKGROUND: USDOT envisions a future transportation ecosystem where CDA complements both human-driven and automated vehicles to improve roadway safety, mobility, and operational efficiency. While standalone vehicle automation has advanced, it continues to struggle with complex edge cases such as occlusion, complex merging, or identifying pedestrians hidden behind buildings at corners, and vehicle sensors alone cannot adequately resolve these issues. Prior USDOT-supported research projects have successfully demonstrated the technical proof-of-concept at technology readiness levels (TRL) of 3-5 for CDA applications in laboratory and closed environments. However, most new vehicles are not equipped with CDA capabilities and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) remain reluctant to integrate these technologies into production lines due to a lack of consumer awareness and unclear regulatory, policy, and institutional frameworks. This acquisition seeks to build on foundational CDA research by bridging the gap between research concepts and commercial viability. There is a critical need to develop and test pre-production, industry-led prototypes at a TRL of 6-7, to validate that the data shared between vehicles and roadside infrastructure is accurate, secure, and reliable enough to support functional safety. By demonstrating CDA technologies in operational conditions, researchers will gain a better understanding of cooperative systems and if they are more valuable in terms of improving roadway safety, than standalone automation or vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technologies alone. PURPOSE: The purpose of this requirement is to demonstrate industry-led CDA prototypes in controlled and real-world conditions in order to generate data-driven insights that will support the development of a national strategy to deploy CDA across rural, suburban, and urban roadway systems. This effort prioritizes industry-ready CDA technology for use cases with clear safety and/or mobility benefit potential, specifically focusing on: (1) Work Zone Management, (2) Traffic Incident Management, (3) Cooperative Perception, and/or (4) Emergency/Transit Vehicle Awareness. Contractors will first validate the prototype's interoperability, functional safety, and cybersecurity in a relevant, controlled testbed environment. Following successful controlled testing, the effort will progress into a small scale real-world demonstration on public roads with mixed traffic to validate operational readiness and generate data-driven insights.

title: High-Cut Ballistic Helmets
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Subject: High-Cut Ballistic Helmets Notice Type: Request for Information / Sources Sought 1. PURPOSE This Request for Information (RFI) is being issued for informational and market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a Request for Quotation (RFQ), nor is it considered to be a commitment by the Government/Issuing Agency. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors and manufacturers capable of providing Berry Amendment Compliant commercial High-Cut Ballistic Helmets. All quantities listed within this RFI are estimated quantities and are subject to change. The contract shall be issued as a Firm Fixed Price, Indefinite Quantity/Indefinite Delivery (IDIQ) type contract with up to five (5) separately priced tiers, spanning 12 months each. 2. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS All proposed solutions must meet the following general requirements: Berry Amendment Compliance: All items, materials, and manufacturing processes must be 100% Berry Amendment compliant. Proof of compliance will be required. Helmets that must meet or exceed ballistic performance NIJ Level III-A (according to NIJ STD 0106.01/0108.01) standard. Sizing: All helmets must be available in Small (S) to Extra-Large (XL) sizes. 3. SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS & ESTIMATED QUANTITIES Estimated Quantity: 2,875 units total to be ordered in any combination of sizes Small to Extra Large (Multiple procurement tiers ranging from 240 to 975 units per tier). Required Features: Must meet or exceed ballistic performance NIJ Level III-A (according to NIJ STD 0106.01/0108.01) standard. Must meet MIL-STD-810G methods/Environmental Conditions. Must fit sizes S-XL. Must be available in ranger green color. Must have accessory mounting system. Must have a customizable fit by being equipped with moveable comfort pads. Must have berry compliant three-piece zorbium foam impact liner. Must have a foam liner that protects against impact and allows for an overhead communications headband/ear protection. Must meet or exceed ACH Blunt Impact Requirement per AR/PD10-02, 16DEC13 Impact liner must have water-resistant film and antimicrobial wicking fabric covering. Must feature a hybrid composite shell which increases strength and provides an optimal fit. Must have a lanyard-compatible Wilcox shroud, which aids in securing any standard NVG mount. Must have a retention system that quickly adjusts to individual head shapes, providing comfort and stability. Hardware must be stainless steel with MIL-DTL-13924D black oxide coating. Side rail accessories must be gloss-reinforced polycarbonate. Must allow one handed adjustment for retention system.4. INSTRUCTIONS FOR SUBMISSION Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement demonstrating their ability to provide the requested items. Submissions should include: Company name, address, Point of Contact (POC), telephone number, and email address. Confirmation of 100% Berry Amendment Compliance for all proposed products. Product specification sheets or literature matching the salient characteristics listed above (without providing pricing). Estimated lead times for the stated estimated quantities. Capability Statements may be sent to Casandra.Rogers@dla.mil through September 28, 2026. Please note: Pricing is not required at this time, as this RFI is for market research purposes.

description: PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) Department of Veterans Affairs Teleradiology Staffing Services SECTION 1 PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND 1.1 Purpose This Performance Work Statement (PWS) establishes the requirements for teleradiology interpretation services to support STAT and routine priority imaging studies at Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) medical facilities. Based on a 12-month analysis of 17,278 STAT priority imaging studies across five VA facilities (June 2025 May 2026), 41.2% of STAT examinations failed to meet required timeliness standards, representing a significant patient safety and care quality risk. The Government requires a qualified contractor to provide licensed radiologist interpretation staffing services during identified high-risk coverage periods to reduce late reporting rates and ensure Veterans receive timely diagnostic care. 1.1 Background Physician personnel shortages and turnover in the Diagnostic Radiology Services at the covered VA medical facilities have created a significant need for additional professional diagnostic radiology interpretive capacity to ensure that both routine and emergent radiology imaging examinations are always available to Veterans. Contracted teleradiologists will provide final radiology interpretations for exams performed during off tours, and in some cases for exams performed during routine tours when other radiologist services are not available or insufficient to meet clinical demand. The use of teleradiology outsourcing provides a highly cost-effective and expeditious alternative to meet ongoing needs across the covered facilities. Data analysis of STAT imaging volume and timeliness identified three critical coverage gaps: Weekday Overnight Gap (Monday Friday, 8:00 PM 7:30 AM): STAT late rates range from 22% to 60% during overnight hours, with volumes averaging 2 10 studies per overnight shift per facility. Weekend Gap (All Day Saturday and Sunday): Saturday and Sunday represent the highest-volume and worst-performing periods, with late rates reaching 63.6% and average STAT volumes of up to 33 studies per day across facilities. Federal Holiday Gap: Federal holidays represent near-complete coverage failures, with late rates of 75 100% on holidays such as Presidents' Day, MLK Day, Labor Day, and New Year's Day across most covered facilities. The covered facilities use electronic image and health record management and distribution systems including CPRS, VistA Imaging, Philips Intellispace PACS, and Nuance PowerScribe. Contractors with prior experience connecting to VISN 4 radiology systems are preferred. 1.3 Covered Facilities The following VA medical facilities are covered under this contract: Facility Address Altoona VAMC 2907 Pleasant Valley Boulevard, Altoona, PA 16602 Erie VAMC 135 East 38th Street, Erie, PA 16504 Lebanon VAMC 1700 South Lincoln Avenue, Lebanon, PA 17042 Philadelphia VAMC 3900 Woodland Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19805 Pittsburgh VAMC 4100 Aliquippa Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15240I was in touch with the CO, Erik Whitaker and CS, David Santiago who will be working on this package and is the current CO/CS for Pitt s current contract. They both confirmed that if we added Pitt and Phila into the PWS, they can order off the contract at a later date and it won t be considered out of scope . Wilmington VAMC 1601 Kirkwood Highway, Wilmington, DE 19805 Wilkes-Barre VAMC 1111 East End Boulevard, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711 * Philadelphia VAMC and Pittsburgh VAMC are not currently placing orders under this contract. However, the awarded vendor must be able to fulfill future orders from these facilities if requested. 1.4 Period of Performance The estimated Period of Performance (POP) for this 5-year contract is from December 31, 2026, to December 30, 2031. SECTION 2 SCOPE OF WORK 2.1 General Scope The Contractor shall provide professional teleradiology staffing services for diagnostic radiology imaging examinations performed at the covered VA medical facilities. Contract services will include off-campus image interpretation via a secure network connection to VA informatics systems, and as needed, providing advice by telephone to clinical providers and radiology technologists regarding protocols or for clarifying questions about radiology exams. The Contractor shall comply with each facility's policies related to reporting of examinations, use of diagnostic codes, and communication of results. The Contractor must be a U.S.-based corporation capable of final interpretation and reporting services via a secure teleradiology network. All services SHALL be performed within the territorial borders of the United States. Contracting to radiologists outside of the territories of the USA is prohibited. The Contractor shall provide all professional personnel and technical support, medical and other equipment, telecommunications, supplies, and supervision necessary to perform, implement, and administer teleradiology services to meet the specific medical needs of the covered facilities. The Contractor is responsible for all Contractor personnel, subcontractors, agents, and anyone acting for or on behalf of the Contractor. 2.2 Modalities Covered The Contractor shall provide interpretation services for the following imaging modalities, which may include imaging of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis, and extremities: Modality Description Priority Facilities CT / CTA Computed Tomography / CT Angiography All facilities highest volume and highest late rate CR / XR Computed/Digital Radiography (plain film) All facilities high weekend/holiday volume DX Digital Radiography All facilities second-highest volume overall MR / MRA Magnetic Resonance Imaging / MR Angiography Wilkes-Barre, Altoona (limited volumes) US Ultrasound Wilmington, Wilkes-Barre, Altoona, Erie, Pittsburgh (limited volumes) Mammography Diagnostic and screening mammography As occasionally requested, Nuclear Medicine / PET-CT General nuclear medicine and PET/CT As occasionally requested, Diagnostic Radiology / Plain Film (Radiology) Computed Tomography (CT) CT Abdomen & Pelvis (W/O or W & W/O) / CT ABD & Pelvis CT Angiographs / Computed Tomography Angiography CT Angio Abd&Pelv w/o&w/dye / CT SBD & Pelv 1/>REGNS CT Abdomen & Pelvis Multiphase CT Angio Abdominal Arteries w/Runoffs Magnetic Resonance Imaging / Magnetic Resonance (MR) Exam Magnetic Resonance Imaging Angio Magnetic Resonance Imaging Prostate / MR Prostate Ultrasound / Ultrasound (US) Ultrasound - Head and Neck (Thyroid) + Transplants / US Head and neck Ultrasound - OB US Arterial Duplex Nuclear Medicine / Nuclear Medicine (NM) Positron Emission Tomography (PET CT)/Position Emission Tomography (PET)/CT 2D Mammography single breast exam / 2D Mammo 3D Mammography single breast exam / 3D Mammo MRI Cardiac (cpt codes 75557, 75559, 75561, 75563)/Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Cardiac CT Heart (cpt codes 75572, 75573, 75574) MR Abdomen Exams 2.3 Priority Classification Studies transmitted under this contract shall be classified as either STAT or Routine: STAT: All imaging performed on inpatients and Emergency Department (ED) patients will be considered STAT. Other outpatient studies will be considered STAT if they have been ordered as such or if an expedited interpretation is requested by facility staff. Routine: Outpatient studies not otherwise designated as STAT, with a preferred turnaround of 24 hours and a mandatory turnaround of 48 hours. The Contractor shall not commingle STAT VA studies with routine or non-VA workloads in a manner that degrades turnaround time performance. SECTION 3 COVERAGE PERIODS AND VOLUME ESTIMATES 3.1 Required Coverage Windows The Contractor shall provide continuous radiologist coverage during the following periods. Less often, teleradiology services may also be requested during regular business hours (Monday Friday, 8:00 AM 4:30 PM) during staffing shortages; the Contractor shall accommodate such requests when operationally feasible. 3.1.1 Weekday Overnight Coverage

A combined Synopsis/Solicitation is being issued for the purchase of the UNDERSHIRT, OLIVE DRAB, MC. ITEM: Undershirt, Olive Drab, MC PGC: 02424--NSN: 8420-01-450-0048(s) EA The Solicitation for the purchase of the Undershirt, Olive Drab, MC will result with the intent of the Government to award one contract. The RFP and proposed contract(s) will be issued as 100% Small Business Set-Aside. Only small business firms may submit offers for this acquisition. The Small Business Set-Aside will result in firm fixed price contract or contracts in accordance with FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items. The Undershirt, Olive Drab, MC is classified under Federal Supply Classification (FSC) Code 8420. The Department of Defense (DoD) publishes an annual list of product categories for which the Federal Prison Industries� (FPI) share of the DoD market is greater than five percent, which is considered a significant market share and must be competed. FSC 8420 is currently identified on this list, FPI is considered to have a significant market share. In accordance with 8.602(a)(4), agencies shall include Federal Prison Industries, Inc. (FPI), in the solicitation process and consider a timely offer from FPI/UNICOR in accordance with the specifications and evaluation factors as outlined in the solicitation. The resultant contract will be an award of a 60-month contract consisting of five (5) 12-month price tier periods. Each tier shall be for a 12-month period. This proposed buy will result in a negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type contract(s). This acquisition is a 60-month contract consisting of five (5) 12-month price tier periods. The quantities will be as follows: Quantity Total Acquisition: Contract Guaranteed Min: 55,776 each Annual Estimated Quantity: 222,816 each per tier Contract Maximum: 1,392,600 each all tiers combined The resultant contract(s) will have a Five (5) year ordering period. Within the Five (5) year ordering period, there will be Five (5) 12-month price Tier periods. This proposed buy will result in a negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type Contract(s). The quantities for the acquisition are listed above for the total acquisition. This proposed buy will result with the intent of the Government to award up to one (1) negotiated Indefinite Delivery Type contract. Best Value / Trade Off / Source Selection Procedures will be utilized in making the proposed award(s), and as a result, Technical Proposals are required. Technical and Past Performance, when combined, are more important than cost or price. Evaluation factors are as follows in descending order of importance: Product Demonstration Model (PDM) in accordance with CID A-A-50013H, dated September 9, 2024 and Past Performance/Performance Confidence Assessment. Evaluation of the PDMs will effectively indicate the contractor�s comprehension of the item�s technical requirements and their ability to manufacture the items in accordance with the Purchase Description.
