title: C1DA--A/E Services Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360 Project Number: 640A0-27-103
description: This is a Call for SF 330s. Please read the entire document. The Department of Veterans Affairs VA Palo Alto Menlo Park Healthcare System, CA is seeking Architectural/Engineering Firms to submit Standard Form (SF) 330 for Project 640A0-27-103, Replace Patient Lifts B331, B348, & B360. The project will be located at the Palo Alto Menlo Park VA Campus, 3801 Miranda Ave, Palo Alto, California 94304. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The VA Palo Alto - Menlo Park Division needs A/E design services to replace/install 141 new ceiling-mounted patient lifts and extend 24 existing lifts for full room + bathroom coverage in CLC Buildings 331, 348, and 360. B348/B360 private rooms have no lift; B331 has outdated linear lifts; B360 needs bathroom coverage extensions + 30 motor upgrades. A/E Requirement: Full field survey above/below ceiling, structural/SE seismic analysis and HCAI OPM, MEP/electrical, fire protection, phasing plan for occupied patient rooms, Revit BIM, specs, and independent cost estimate. Construction cost shall not exceed $16.4M for all work in B331, B348 & B360, requiring site investigations, block diagrams, and full design deliverables at 35%, 65%, 95%, 100% and final production per VA Master Specs and all applicable codes, including cost estimates, phased construction documents, and 5-year construction period services including RFI responses, submittal reviews, weekly meetings, site inspections, and as-builts, all to be completed within a 266-day design period. The design shall also substantially meet the VA design criteria as listed in VA design guides and manuals, which can be found on the web at the VA Office of Facilities Management technical information library site address: http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL The design effort shall also include review of and assurance of compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, including development and submission of all documents, reports, and activities necessary to obtain the required compliance. The contract work requires multiple disciplines. The Prime firm shall be a licensed/registered professional firm in any state in the United States, and the lead designer in each discipline must be registered/licensed in any state. Exception: The Structural Engineer of Record (SEOR) participating in the structural/seismic design must be licensed in the State of California and must have current authority to use the title of Structural Engineer (SE) in California, per H-18-8 and VA Directive 7512. Disciplines required include, but are not limited to: Architectural, Civil, Interior Design, Structural (CA SE), HVAC, Plumbing, Electrical, Fire Protection, Construction Cost Estimating, Signage/Wayfinding, Landscaping and Geotechnical. Include any additional disciplines that may be necessary on SF 330. SF 330 Part 1F Example Projects; present all relevant VA projects first. Include in block 21 the contract number for all federal projects. Do not include the CPARS reports for federal projects. SELECTION CRITERIA Selection of firms for interviews and negotiations shall be based on an evaluation of the submitted SF-330s based on the selection criteria listed below in a descending order of precedence. SF-330s, Part I may be accompanied by any other evidence of experience and capabilities the applicant considers relevant. Part II shall be submitted for each proposed consultant s office involved. Additional Evaluation Factors: Previous experience with patient lift design in a hospital setting and length of and role in that experience. If no patient lift design, then required hospital setting design experience and associated phasing requirements in an occupied Community Living Center (CLC) / acute care environment. Experience with patient lift products, makers, and providers (e.g., ARJO and similar ceiling-mounted systems) is desired and will be evaluated. Design for construction staging/phasing in an active, occupied healthcare environment, including ICRA/ILSM measures, is required. Selection Criteria descriptions are provided below. Experience of the prime firm, consultant firms, and proposed designers. Prime firms must have proven experience in health care design through construction administration. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence in hospital design with the ability to design and administer projects within a complex, active healthcare environment with stringent seismic requirements in the State of California. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time and the ability to adhere to schedules. Provide current workload capability of the prime firm, proposed consultants, and designers. Literature should be included to demonstrate the prime firm s ability to meet scheduled deadlines. This will allow the Government to determine the availability of experienced personnel during the performance period of the contract as well as the capacity to complete the work required. Past Performance on contracts with respect to cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules during design and construction phases (prime firm). Geographical location and knowledge of the locality of the project. This requirement considers the prime firm s familiarity with the applicable geographic area s architectural standards and codes, building codes, environmental regulations, soil conditions, and seismic requirements within the Palo Alto Menlo Park area. The prime firm must be able to respond to and be on-site within a twenty-four-hour window. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: No more than eighty (80) pages Font size no smaller than 10 Size of emails not to exceed 10 MB. If more than one email is sent, number the emails in the subject line as 1 of 2, 2 of 2. Complete and return VAAR 852.219-76 VA Notice of Limitation on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (attached) Subject line of the email shall state Company Name | Response to 36C26126Q1139_1 | email 1 of 2 (if necessary). In the body of the email, include Prime Company Name; UEI Number; email address and phone number of primary points of contact. DUE DATE FOR SF 330 Firms that meet the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit required SF 330s by 12:00 P.M. (PDT) Monday, September 28, 2026, to Alex Arter at alex.arter@va.gov. It is the intent of the Contracting Officer to make a single firm-fixed-price contract award under this solicitation.

Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Defense Commissary Agency is seeking for solutions for Planogramming-Assortment Planning SaaS Solution The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is a component of the Department of War (DoW) that provides enterprise-wide mission support to all United States (U.S.) uniformed services, including the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, and Coast Guard, in both continental United States (CONUS) and outside of the continental United States (OCONUS) locations. DeCA�s mission is to deliver a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings to military personnel and their families. DeCA operates a global system of 235 commissaries across 45 states, 13 countries, and two U.S. territories, with approximately 3,000 checkout lanes. To support modern retail operations, DeCA requires a robust, integrated planogramming and assortment planning Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution that enables data-driven merchandising decisions, optimizes retail space utilization, improves category performance, and supports efficient planogram development, maintenance, and execution across its worldwide network. DeCA�s Category Management team manages over 200 product categories across approximately 235 globally dispersed store locations. Historically, Category Managers have expended significant manual effort building, updating, and maintaining product assortments and physical planograms. This process is highly complex due to the unique architectural layouts, localized merchandising requirements, and varying store sizes of each individual commissary. To modernize operations, DeCA requires a comprehensive, integrated Planogramming-Assortment Planning Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. title: W912DY26QA327 NAD-AF Fuels Program PMCM Bridge
description: SYNOPSIS OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACT The U.S. Army Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville (CEHNC), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for Fuel Program Preventive Maintenance and Corrective Maintenance (PMCM) services supporting the North Atlantic Division�Air Force (NAD-AF). The contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, quality control, transportation, supplies, vehicles, tools, materials, facilities, equipment, and incidentals necessary to perform preventive and corrective maintenance on capitalized federal petroleum facilities and petroleum systems. Services shall ensure these systems remain compliant with all applicable codes, criteria, regulations, and laws, including United Facilities Criteria (UFC) 3-460-03. The requirement supports sites throughout the North Atlantic Division, including, but not limited to, Lakehurst; Andrews Site #1; Warren Grove Range #1; Barnes MAP (ANG) Site #1; Bradley IAP Site #1; Burlington IAP Site #1; Bangor IAP Site #1; Hancock Field Site #1; EWVRA Sheppard Field; Pittsburgh IAP (ANG) Site #1; PGH IAP ARS Site #1; New Castle Airport; Fort Indiantown Gap AGS Area #1; McLaughlin ANGB (Yeager APT Site #1); Langley AFB Site #1; Hanscom AFB Site #1; Martin State Airport Site #1; McGuire ANGB; McGuire AFB; Niagara Falls Site #1 AF Reserve; Harrisburg IAP ANG Site #1; Otis ANG Base Site #1; Pease ANGB NH Site #1; Quonset State Airport Site #1; Schenectady ANG MAP Site #1; Stewart IAP Site #1; Francis S. Gabreski Airport Site #1; Atlantic City IAP Site #1; Westover ARB Site #1; Horsham Air Guard Station; Dix; Fort Eustis; Dover AFB Site #1; Bangor Lease Land Site #4; and JB Anacostia Bolling. The anticipated period of performance is 336 days, structured as a 66-day base period followed by three 90-day option periods: Option Year 1, Option Year 2, and Option Year 3. The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA), through USACE CEHNC, has a continued requirement for preventive and corrective maintenance of Air Force fuel systems within the NAD-AF area of responsibility. CEHNC executes this maintenance in accordance with UFC 3-460-03, which establishes procedures and standards for maintenance of petroleum fuel systems. This work is critical to sustaining operational fuel systems and robust fueling capability in support of Defense Logistics Agency�Energy (DLA-E) capitalized federal petroleum facilities and petroleum systems across the NAD-AF area of responsibility. The work will be structured around performance-based outcomes. Preventive maintenance services include maintaining federal petroleum facilities and petroleum systems to ensure compliance with applicable codes, criteria, regulations, and laws of the United States and its outlying areas. These services also include written reports documenting evaluated systems. Corrective maintenance services include service orders for minor repairs to deficiencies affecting petroleum facilities, petroleum systems, and supporting DLA-E capitalized facilities, as well as emergency-response capability necessary to ensure the safe and reliable accomplishment of the applicable fuels delivery mission. Repairs may be requested by each DLA capitalized site for components, equipment, or systems supporting that mission. The scope of services shall be strictly limited to actions essential to maintaining operational readiness and preventing mission degradation during the 48-week period of performance. As outlined in the Performance Work Statement, the work includes scheduled, mission-essential preventive maintenance; necessary corrective maintenance to address system and equipment failures; and response to emergent or unforeseen service requirements critical to sustaining the mission. title: Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) Planogramming-Assortment Planning Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) Solution
description: This Call for Solutions is issued under the Army Open Solicitation W9128Z-25-S-A002. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Defense Commissary Agency is seeking for solutions for Planogramming-Assortment Planning SaaS Solution The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is a component of the Department of War (DoW) that provides enterprise-wide mission support to all United States (U.S.) uniformed services, including the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, and Coast Guard, in both continental United States (CONUS) and outside of the continental United States (OCONUS) locations. DeCA�s mission is to deliver a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings to military personnel and their families. DeCA operates a global system of 235 commissaries across 45 states, 13 countries, and two U.S. territories, with approximately 3,000 checkout lanes. To support modern retail operations, DeCA requires a robust, integrated planogramming and assortment planning Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution that enables data-driven merchandising decisions, optimizes retail space utilization, improves category performance, and supports efficient planogram development, maintenance, and execution across its worldwide network. DeCA�s Category Management team manages over 200 product categories across approximately 235 globally dispersed store locations. Historically, Category Managers have expended significant manual effort building, updating, and maintaining product assortments and physical planograms. This process is highly complex due to the unique architectural layouts, localized merchandising requirements, and varying store sizes of each individual commissary. To modernize operations, DeCA requires a comprehensive, integrated Planogramming-Assortment Planning Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution. The Call for Solutions document, submission requirements can be found in the Attachments section below.

For the upper strobe light, the power supply is located inside the fuselage below the strobe light, mounted on the side of the air conditioning duct.
